assumptions: Workbook values are organizer-supplied synthetic planning limits, not actual airport data.
One runway and two candidate spare gates are a declared subset of the airport inventory. Other gates are unavailable to this decision.
Background movements are a complete synthetic traffic schedule within the planning and capacity windows; filtered DOT rows are not a queue.
M denotes Large; S/H/L denote Super/Heavy/Small. Same-runway departure time minima are an explicitly declared arrival simulation proxy; nautical-mile separation is not modeled.
Narrowbody class, 4000 kg trip fuel, 20 kg/min taxi burn and 50 kg uncertainty allowance are synthetic inputs. Arrival spare fuel includes the reserve and contingency, a conservative interpretation.
Flight duty ends at gate arrival. Report time and ground crew report times are synthetic; ground maximum duty ends at t=7200, an additional declared scenario cap.
Gate-change notice is measured from t=0 to landing, conservatively before gate arrival. Routes, service targets, connections, reservations and equipment availability are synthetic.
